At least, that's what I was informed earlier, much earlier on this year, much earlier on this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's my understanding that that's a different archive. It may have had to do with Muslim documents. This is a VRS and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. It's a VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we're talking about two different things but I'll confirm that for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Maybe, but I think we're talking about the same one because this was the latest acquisition of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We don't have this material. We have just gotten access to it within the last two weeks. There are people that are at this archives looking at it, and they have scanners, and what they bring back will be in our possession soon, but as -- as yet, all we have is rumours and -- but there's so many collections out there that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. McCloskey, but I would suggest that you consult with Ms. Sellers or Mr. Di Fazio and they can indicate to you whether they are talking of the same collection or not. I am pretty confident that we are talking about the same collection because I'm not aware of a fresh Banja Luka discovery since -- since then. But anyway, it's up to you. But I do appreciate you bringing up this issue because it may turn up to extremely important later on. On the Defence side, any one of you would like to raise any other matter that we have not dealt with? None? So -- yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It just slipped my mind but it came back. I just discussed this issue with the Prosecution, and just for the record, I would like to have their position regarding the pre-trial brief that they have already filed. I mean, what I have in mind is that there will be some changes in the indictment -- there has been some changes in the indictment, and I would like to have the information whether they have any intention to, I don't know, to amend their pre-trial brief, to make any changes in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good -- good point, Mr. Lazarevic. Of course I will not speak for the Prosecution. And in fact I will ask first the Prosecutor to respond to that and then I will tell you what is very relevant for the Trial Chamber at the present moment. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would certainly like to think what you hear is relevant, Your Honour, because we remain -- we would like to be able to provide you any information you think you need relating to the -- the new facts, basically, as we see it. If there is some clarification that is needed, we would gladly fill those holes or those gaps and I will certainly find out from the Defence what they would like to hear about. We have our marching orders on a few things already, but if there's anything else, yeah, we're able and willing to provide more information, but we should leave something for the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was pretty sure that that was what I was going to hear from you. The position of the Trial Chamber, if necessary, will be made in due course, obviously, and a lot depends also on how we are going to decide the outstanding issues in the wake of your motion and those of the other two accused. However, you will recall the Status Conference of -- May Status Conference when I hinted for the first time at proceeding with asking the Prosecution to prepare these proofing charts. My idea of proofing charts at the time was that it is a perfection of the pre-trial brief. Basically, it's reproducing the pre-trial brief in a more visible and more understandable and more practical manner. So ultimately, we will be discussing this and come back to both of you, particularly to the Prosecution, and indicate whether there is a need to have an updated pre-trial brief or whether this matter can be addressed fully in the -- in the proofing chart. We can't tell you what it is because we haven't discussed it enough amongst ourselves to reach a decision, but it is something that we have been thinking about. And thank you, Mr. Lazarevic, for raising the matter. Anything else? Any further issues? I see none, so we bring to an end this Status Conference today at half past 5.00. We will reconvene on Thursday. I think it's in the afternoon, Thursday at 2.15. With us we will have Judge Stole from Norway as the Reserve Judge, and we can have the Pre-Trial Conference. Please try to prepare as much as you can to have that exercise, make it as easy as possible. And I wish to show the Trial Chamber's gratitude for the way you have been conducting yourselves in preparation for the trial. I think it's very constructive, very cooperative, and we really appreciate -- we really appreciate that. I thank you. Please, God willing, we'll meet on Thursday. Thank you, and good evening.
